Martin Bauer asked me to post this:

Mathematics at a Turning Point: AI, Research, and the Next Generation—An zoom panel on mathematical practice, graduate training, and careers in the age of AI 

Summary: Over the past year, AI’s abilities in mathematical reasoning have advanced at an unprecedented pace, reshaping how mathematics is discovered, verified, and taught. These developments raise pressing questions for our community: How should we credit AI-assisted results? What will be the effects on graduate education? And how can we still offer a vision and meaningful opportunities for young researchers? These and related questions will be explored in an online panel discussion on September 25 featuring E. Aldrovandi (FSU), J. Avigad (CMU), T. Feng (Berkeley), J. Gómez-Serrano (Brown), A. Kontorovich (Rutgers University) and R. Ward (UT Austin). 
Registration: More information and registration are available at: https://www.math.fsu.edu/~bauer/AI-Math/turning-point-2026.html
